lineage.strategy: Move from issuer-index headline metrics to SEC-filed backlog composition, cash conversion and liquidity evidence.

observations.fact: Powell's SEC filing reports $2.4 billion of backlog at June 30, 2026, up 73% from September 2025; commercial/other industrial represented 40%, while oil and gas excluding petrochemical and electric utility each represented 24%.
Bookings net of cancellations and scope reductions increased 112% to $1.9 billion for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $879.7 million a year earlier.

Operating activities provided $195.0 million of cash for the first nine months of FY2026 versus $106.9 million a year earlier; cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $633.6 million and no amounts were borrowed under the U.S. revolver.

risks.risk: Cash conversion depends on project volume, margins, working-capital requirements and milestone-payment timing; a record backlog therefore does not guarantee smooth revenue or cash realization.

unknowns.unknown: The filing does not disclose realized future margin by backlog cohort or exact cancellation/modification sensitivity for the largest projects.

recommendation: Use SEC-filed backlog composition, bookings, operating cash flow and liquidity to strengthen underwriting while explicitly preserving project-conversion and working-capital timing risk.
